title: Activation sprint — daily greenroom notes & fallback matrix
content:
Purpose: quick operational diary and decision matrix for the 2-week activation sprint with Customer X. Focus: safe ramp from test traffic to 100rps production window, clear rollback triggers, and daily greenroom cadence. This doc lives as the single source for day-by-day staffing, runbooks, and fallback actions during the trial activation.

Summary notes (TL;DR):
- Goal: demonstrate stable 95th p99 latency < 300ms for text-gen route, and < 50ms for embedding lookups at 100rps sustained.
- Acceptance criteria: 72h of steady-state at target load with <1% error budget, no quality regressions on eval prompt set.
- Primary risks: model OOM under long sequences, KV cache thrash on mixed-length requests, upstream tokenization mismatch.
- Primary mitigation levers: route small/large seqs to different model variants (opt-xxs / opt-lr), enable per-customer prefix caching, temporary throttle to dedicated pool.

Daily greenroom schedule (standup + monitoring rotation):
- 08:30 UTC: pre-shift sync (15m) — quick ops checklist, confirm deployments and monitoring hooks. Owner: Aisha R.
- 09:00–12:00 UTC: morning monitoring window (traffic ramp). Ops: Marco C. / Priya N.
- 12:00–13:00 UTC: mid-day health review + stakeholder update (customer PM on call). Ops: Tomas A.
- 16:00–18:00 UTC: evening ramp and stability confirmation. Ops: Emily Z.
- 18:30 UTC: post-shift handoff note, publish greenroom log. Owner: on-shift engineer.

Pre-launch checklist (must pass before any traffic ramp):
- [ ] Canary deployed 2 replicas to dedicated pool (k8s deployment tag: customer-x-canary-20241115).
- [ ] KV cache warmers executed with canonical prefix set (scripts/warm_cache.sh).
- [ ] Synthetic trace run against canary (ab: 1000 requests, 95th p99 < target).
- [ ] Alerting configured: latency p95/p99, error rate, token cost spike, GPU memory OOM.
- [ ] Run smoke evals for correctness on SRE-approved prompt set.
- [ ] Customer forward-proxy TLS cert verified and KMS integration smoke test passed.

Day-by-day activation cadence (high level):
- Day -2: environment freeze; dependency cutover; share runbook; dry run with SE team.
- Day -1: final performance baseline; run synthetic load; confirm rollback scripts.
- Day 0 (go-live): 5rps -> 20rps -> 50rps -> 100rps over 3 hours. Hold at each step for 30m and run health checks.
- Day 1–3: observation window; run controlled traffic bursts; collect evals; adjust batching settings if token cost rises >20%.
- Day 4–7: extend steady-state tests (24h windows), enable customer traffic shaping to replicate real user patterns.
- Day 8–14: scale test to sustained peak; begin incremental canary promotion (50% -> 100% on dedicated pool).

Task tracker (shorthand):
- infra/ops: deploy-canary (Marco C.) — target: Day -1 complete. Jira SE-2142.
- se: prompt-evals (Priya N.) — run suite, report quality regressions. Jira SE-2145.
- dev: quant-profiles (Tomas A.) — provide two quant/latency trade-off builds by Day 1. Jira SE-2150.
- sde: traffic-router (Emily Z.) — policy for short/long routing + fallback to hosted small model. Jira SE-2161.
- security: cert-kms-check (Aisha R.) — confirm HSM key access and audit.

Fallback matrix (failure mode -> immediate action -> owner -> rollback action):
- Failure: p99 latency spikes above 600ms for >5m
  - Immediate action: divert traffic to lower-latency variant (opt-xxs), scale up batching workers with soft-limit. Owner: Emily Z.
  - Rollback: switch traffic back to previous model tag and scale dedicated pool down to pre-ramp size. Command: scripts/traffic_shift.sh --to previous-tag.
- Failure: GPU OOM on canary nodes
  - Immediate action: drain pod, set node as cordoned, reduce max_sequence_length via runtime override. Owner: Marco C.
  - Rollback: revert to smaller quantized model variant and cut traffic by 50%. Command: kubectl rollout undo deploy/customer-x-canary.
- Failure: sustained >2% error rate (5xx or malformed outputs)
  - Immediate action: enable fail-open to host-model stub for non-critical paths, pause new sessions. Owner: Priya N.
  - Rollback: route all traffic to hosted API fallback (route flag: fallback-hosted=true).
- Failure: Quality regression detected on eval set (metric drop > 3%)
  - Immediate action: trigger canary abort; collect debug traces; open incident. Owner: Priya N.
  - Rollback: restore previous model version and invalidate cache. Command: model-manager rollback --customer customer-x --to=2024-11-10

Escalation and contacts:
- SE on-call: Marco Chen (+1-415-555-0192, Slack: @marco).
- Infra SRE: Tomas Alvarez (tomas@redwood.ai, PagerDuty: SRE-pd).
- Product lead: Aisha Reynolds (aisha@redwood.ai).
- Customer PM (Customer X): Jenna Park (jenna@customerx.com).

Monitoring dashboard checklist (confirm before each ramp):
- App metrics: request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, mean tokens per request.
- Infra metrics: GPU mem usage, kernel time, host CPU steal.
- Cost signals: tokens billed per minute, cache hit ratio.
- Health: error rates by route, runtime exceptions, degrader triggers.

Quick runbook snippets (copy into terminal during incidents):
- Shift traffic to fallback model: ./scripts/traffic_shift.sh --to=opt-xxs-fallback --percent=100 --reason=\"latency-spike\"
- Drain problematic node: kubectl cordon <node-name> && kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- Re-enable cache warmers: ./scripts/warm_cache.sh --prefix customer-x --parallel=4
- Snapshot traces for incident: ./scripts/pull_traces.sh --since=10m --tags customer-x > /tmp/incident-trace.json

Risk heatmap (quick):
- High: long-sequence OOMs, cache thrash
- Medium: tokenization mismatches, customer-side agent misconfigs
- Low: minor latency regressions within error budget

Open questions / unknowns (to resolve before Day 0):
- Can Customer X accept temporary routing to hosted fallback in their SLA? (ask Sales/legal)
- What is the realistic token length distribution for their peak user flows? Need sampled logs.
- Are there any IP allowlist constraints that will block our warmers?

Notes to self / informal reminders (choppy):
- if cache hit < 60% during ramp, try per-customer sticky cache keys, but watch eviction.
- remember to update billing tag on canary runs or finance will freak (tag: customer-x-poc-202411).
- keep a short running diary in #se-greenroom Slack thread; paste the final daily summary to Confluence.

Post-activation deliverables (owner):
- 72h post-mortem + metrics export (Marco C.)
- Quality report and recommend model variant (Priya N.)
- Cost/latency trade-off writeup for customer-facing doc (Aisha R.)

Revision history:
- 2024-11-15 created by Aisha Reynolds (initial outline)
- 2024-11-28 added fallback matrix and runbook snippets (Marco Chen)
- 2025-01-10 updated acceptance criteria and monitoring checklist after dry run (Priya Nair)

Checklist: Ready-for-review? YES (confirm with product and SRE before moving to final).

-- end of activation-sprint greenroom notes --
